questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Let |A| = 4 and |B| = 3. How many onto (surjective) functions exist from A to B?
questions.explanationEn: By inclusion-exclusion, onto functions from m=4 to n=3 elements = 3^4 - C(3,1)*2^4 + C(3,2)*1^4 = 81 - 48 + 3 = 36.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: For a Binomial random variable X ~ B(n = 20, p = 0.3), what is the variance of X?
questions.explanationEn: For Binomial(n, p), Var(X) = n * p * (1 - p) = 20 * 0.3 * 0.7 = 4.2.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: A connected simple planar graph has 10 vertices and 16 edges. Into how many regions (including the unbounded outer region) does a planar embedding divide the plane?
questions.explanationEn: By Euler's formula for connected planar graphs, V - E + F = 2 => 10 - 16 + F = 2 => F = 8 regions.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: What is the order of the element 4 in the additive group (Z_10, +_10)?
questions.explanationEn: The order of k in Z_n is n / gcd(k, n) = 10 / gcd(4, 10) = 10 / 2 = 5. Indeed, 5 * 4 = 20 ≡ 0 (mod 10).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: What is the value of lim_{x -> 0} (sin(5x) / tan(2x))?
questions.explanationEn: Rewrite as (sin(5x)/(5x)) * (2x/tan(2x)) * (5/2). As x -> 0, both trigonometric ratios approach 1, yielding 5/2.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following functions is/are continuous at x = 0?
optionsEn: f(x) = x * sin(1/x) for x != 0, and f(0) = 0
g(x) = sin(x)/x for x != 0, and g(0) = 1
questions.explanationEn: By squeeze theorem, lim_{x->0} x*sin(1/x) = 0 = f(0) (A). Also lim_{x->0} sin(x)/x = 1 = g(0) (B), and |x| is continuous everywhere (D). 1/x diverges at 0 (C false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Let G be a finite group of prime order p. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: G has exactly two subgroups (the trivial subgroup and G itself).
Every non-identity element of G is a generator of G.
questions.explanationEn: By Lagrange's theorem, subgroup orders divide p, so only orders 1 and p exist (C). Any non-identity element generates a subgroup of order > 1, hence all of G (D), making G cyclic (A) and thus Abelian (B).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following sets of logical connectives is NOT functionally complete?
questions.explanationEn: Using only {∧, ∨}, any formula evaluates to True when all inputs are True (monotonicity), so negation ¬p cannot be expressed. Thus {∧, ∨} is not functionally complete.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following graphs is/are planar?
questions.explanationEn: By Kuratowski's theorem, K_5 and K_{3,3} are the minimal non-planar graphs. K_4 and every K_{2,n} (such as K_{2,5}) are planar.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: What is the determinant of the upper triangular matrix [[2, 5, 7], [0, -3, 4], [0, 0, 5]]?
questions.explanationEn: The determinant of a triangular matrix is the product of its main diagonal entries: 2 * (-3) * 5 = -30.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Let S = {p -> q, q -> r, ¬r}. Which of the following formulas can be validly inferred from S?
questions.explanationEn: From q -> r and ¬r, Modus Tollens gives ¬q (A). From p -> q and ¬q, Modus Tollens gives ¬p (B). From p -> q and q -> r, Hypothetical Syllogism gives p -> r (C).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: In a group of 4 people, assuming 365 equally likely birthdays and independence, what is the probability that ALL 4 people have distinct birthdays?
questions.explanationEn: The 1st person has 365/365 choices, 2nd has 364/365, 3rd has 363/365, 4th has 362/365. Product = (365 * 364 * 363 * 362) / 365^4.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Let X ~ Normal(μ = 10, σ^2 = 16). Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: The standard deviation of X is 4.
Z = (X - 10)/4 follows the standard normal distribution N(0, 1).
questions.explanationEn: σ = sqrt(16) = 4 (A). A normal distribution is symmetric about its mean μ = 10, so P(X > 10) = 0.5 (B). Standardizing gives Z ~ N(0, 1) (C). E[(X - 10)^2] = Var(X) = 16, not 4 (D is false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Which closed-form generating function generates the sequence a_n = 3^n for n >= 0?
questions.explanationEn: The geometric series Σ_{n=0}^∞ (3x)^n converges to 1 / (1 - 3x) for |x| < 1/3.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: What is the closed-form solution of the recurrence a_n = 4 a_{n-1} - 4 a_{n-2} for n >= 2, with initial conditions a_0 = 1 and a_1 = 6?
questions.explanationEn: Characteristic equation: r^2 - 4r + 4 = (r - 2)^2 = 0 (repeated root r = 2). General form: a_n = (A + Bn)*2^n. From a_0 = 1 => A = 1. From a_1 = (1 + B)*2 = 6 => B = 2. Hence a_n = (1 + 2n)*2^n.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: For an n×n matrix A with all entries equal to 1 (i.e., A = J_n), what are the eigenvalues of A?
optionsEn: 1 with multiplicity 1, and 0 with multiplicity n - 1
n with multiplicity 1, and 0 with multiplicity n - 1
questions.explanationEn: Since all rows of J_n are identical, rank(J_n) = 1, so 0 is an eigenvalue of multiplicity n - 1. The remaining eigenvalue equals trace(J_n) = n (with eigenvector [1, 1, ..., 1]^T).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: What is the maximum number of edges in a simple disconnected graph on 8 vertices?
questions.explanationEn: A disconnected graph on n vertices has maximum edges when it consists of K_{n-1} plus 1 isolated vertex: C(n-1, 2) = C(7, 2) = 7*6/2 = 21 edges.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Let G be a simple undirected graph with n vertices and adjacency matrix A. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: The (i, j)-th entry of A^k equals the number of walks of length k from vertex i to vertex j.
A is always a symmetric matrix.
The trace of A is always 0.
The sum of entries in row i of A equals the degree of vertex i.
questions.explanationEn: For a simple undirected graph, A is symmetric (B) with 0s on the diagonal so trace(A) = 0 (C), row i sums to deg(i) (D), and (A^k)_{ij} counts walks of length k between i and j (A).
